exchanges.author: c_doug
exchanges.body: Great week. Can you rough out a pitch calendar for the rest of November? Let's get back to good news.

exchanges.author: c_teresa
exchanges.subject: Listening session on children's mental health
exchanges.body: Ms. Mathers, the Eastside Health Coalition represents 22 neighborhood groups. Families we work with are excited about the new hospital and have a lot to say about what children's mental health care should look like. Would Prairie Bend hold a listening session with us in December? Teresa Banks, Director

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Dear Ms. Banks, thank you, we'd welcome that. I'm connecting you with Hannah Voss, who leads the Foundation, and our director of media relations, Doug Brenner, so we can bring the right clinical and planning leaders. Could you send two or three December dates that work for your families, and whether evenings are best? Erin Mathers

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Hi Kim, Ruth Kessler can do Monday at 10 a.m. by phone. I'll send her number privately Monday morning and join the call. Erin

exchanges.author: c_luis
exchanges.subject: Re: Sit-down with Dr. Ellison today?
exchanges.body: OK. We'll take Dr. Whitley Wednesday 11/11 at 2 p.m. on ED volumes and staffing. Luis

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Great, Dr. Whitley is confirmed for Wednesday 11/11 at 2 p.m. at the ED entrance; I'll meet your crew there. Erin

exchanges.author: c_hannah
exchanges.subject: Re: Ruth for KPRB
exchanges.body: Ruth says yes: Monday 10 a.m. by phone works for her. Please prep her. Hannah

exchanges.author: c_ruth
exchanges.subject: Thank you
exchanges.body: Erin, yesterday was lovely, thank you for taking such care with Dad's story. Could you send me links to the coverage? Ruth

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Ruth, thank you, it was an honor to tell his story. Highlights: KPRB's 'Gift will bring children's psychiatric care home', the Prairie Business Journal, KNEB 10 and WKLN 7, plus AP and Becker's nationally; links are in the attached summary. I'll call you Monday at 9:30 to prepare for the 10:00 KPRB interview: about 10 minutes, mostly about your father and why this matters. Erin

exchanges.author: c_tasha
exchanges.subject: Urgent care launch ideas, need your OK
exchanges.body: Hi Erin! For the Hickman urgent care opening I'd like to (1) ask all our staff to leave 5-star Google reviews this week so we start strong, and (2) have Jordan Lake (local influencer, 40k followers, we're paying $1,500) film a 'day in the life' inside the clinic on Monday with real patients. OK to go? Tasha

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Love the energy, Tasha, but neither works as planned. (1) Asking staff for 5-star reviews: reviews from employees without a clear disclosure are deceptive under the FTC's rules, and asking only for 5 stars is review gating. Instead, invite patients after their visits to share honest feedback, and staff can share the opening post. (2) Jordan: filming real patients needs each patient's signed MC-7 in advance, and Jordan has to disclose the paid relationship (#ad / 'paid partnership') clearly in every post. Film before opening with staff and actors and it works. Happy to help plan it.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.subject: Pulse item: Kessler gift
exchanges.body: Pulse item (98 words): Largest gift in our history will bring children's psychiatric care home. On Thursday, the Kessler Family Foundation announced a $20 million gift toward the Kessler Children's Behavioral Health Hospital, a 48-bed hospital for children and teens on the Prairie Bend Medical Center campus. With a $12 million state grant, $28 million from PBH and $4 million from other donors, the $64 million project is fully funded and set to open in 2029. Gov. Patricia Hartley joined Dr. Ellison, Ruth Kessler and the Garcia family. Thank you to every caregiver who makes this possible.

exchanges.body: Hello, thank you for covering Thursday's announcement. One correction, please: the headline and story say a $12.5 million state grant; the grant is $12 million (see the release and the Governor's quote). Could you update the online version? Erin Mathers, Prairie Bend Health, 402-555-0110

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.subject: Thank you
exchanges.body: Jamal, thank you and the Governor for being part of Thursday, and for the quick turn on the quote. The Governor's 'care close to home' line led several stories. Coverage summary attached. Erin

versions.content:
# Kessler announcement: coverage summary (through Fri 11/6 9 a.m.)

18 stories, estimated audience 591,000: TV 9 (432,000), print/online 5 (111,000), radio 4 (48,000). AP moved a state story; Becker's picked it up nationally.
Sentiment: 15 positive, 3 neutral, 0 negative. 5 of the 18 also referenced the Ledger's ER story (WKLN 10 p.m., NC9 10 p.m., Ledger online, KPRB evening, KTWO 11/5).
Accuracy: the Star Herald printed a $12.5 million state grant; correction requested 11/6.
Key messages carried: $20 million (18/18), 48 beds (14/18), opening 2029, Governor's 'care close to home'.
